title: Feeding Time Waits for No One
tagline: Forty animals, one schedule, and an enclosure alert that just came through on your radio.

wake_up.text: The zoo doesn't open for hours, but the animals don't know that — feeding and health checks start now, storm or shine.

choices.text: Review last night's health logs before heading out
Head straight out to the enclosures

morning_rounds.text: First rounds of the day: checking water, checking fences, checking that everyone made it through the night the way they should have.

choices.text: Begin feeding

random_moment.text: The quiet hour before the zoo opens has its own particular texture — a little different every morning.

choices.text: The otters are in an unusually playful mood this morning
A stubborn gate latch costs you a few extra minutes
The sunrise over the savanna enclosure stops you for a second

big_cat_feeding.text: Feeding time for the big cats — a precise, careful process that doesn't forgive shortcuts.

choices.text: Follow the full safety protocol exactly, no rushing
Streamline it slightly to save time for the rest of the rounds

vet_check.text: The zoo vet flags a concern about one of the elephants — favoring a leg slightly, nothing dramatic yet, but worth watching.

choices.text: Adjust your rounds to monitor the elephant closely today
Note it and continue with the normal schedule

gates_open.text: The zoo opens for the day. Somewhere behind the scenes, the actual work of caring for forty animals keeps going regardless of how many visitors show up.

choices.text: Continue the morning's work

enclosure_alert.text: Your radio crackles: a latch failure in the primate enclosure, and one of the younger chimps is loose in the service corridor — not near visitors yet, but close, and getting closer every second you spend deciding what to do.

choices.text: Approach calmly yourself with a familiar food reward
Call the full emergency response team before doing anything
Seal the corridor doors first to contain the area
Immediately alert and clear the nearest visitor area

escape_outcome_calm.text: Recognizing you, the chimp comes right to the food reward without any drama at all. Ten minutes after the alert, everyone's exactly where they're supposed to be.

choices.text: Return the chimp and file the incident report

escape_outcome_team.text: The full team arrives and handles it by the book — safe, thorough, and it takes the full protocol's worth of time to actually resolve, which is exactly what the protocol is for.

choices.text: Assist with the recovery

escape_outcome_seal.text: Sealing the corridor first buys real time and certainty — nothing gets worse while you figure out the actual approach, and the recovery that follows goes smoothly.

choices.text: Complete the recovery

escape_outcome_alert.text: Clearing the visitor area first is the safest call for the public, and it costs you time getting to the actual animal — who, it turns out, was never anywhere near visitors at all.

choices.text: Proceed to the recovery

afternoon_visitor_talk.text: A scheduled visitor talk at the big cat enclosure, right after a morning that tested every part of the job.

choices.text: Give the full talk anyway, energy or not
Shorten it today and save your energy

elephant_recheck.text: Time to check on the elephant from this morning's vet note — the limp seems slightly worse by afternoon.

choices.text: Call the vet back for a second look right away
Note it for tomorrow's scheduled check instead

evening_feeding.text: Evening feeding rounds, the zoo emptying out of visitors, the animals settling into their own evening rhythms.

choices.text: Do a thorough final check of every enclosure before leaving
Do the standard evening check and head out

end_shift.text: The zoo goes quiet for the night. Forty animals, all accounted for, all exactly where they're supposed to be.

choices.text: Head home

triumphant.title: Every Animal, Every Time
triumphant.blurb: Every call today was the right one, including the one that could have gone very differently. This is the day the whole team talks about.

steady_hand.title: Solid Day
steady_hand.blurb: No incidents, no drama — just careful, attentive care for every animal, all day long.

ordinary_day.title: Routine Rounds
ordinary_day.blurb: A full day of feeding, checking, and caring for forty animals. Tomorrow's rounds look about the same.

burned_out.title: Running on Empty
burned_out.blurb: You made it through the day, but you're not sure how. This pace, animal after animal, has a real cost.

written_up.title: Incident Review
written_up.blurb: Something about today's handling is going in front of a review board. Every animal is safe. The protocol still needs a look.
